mechanism: Executable world model for an interactive LLM game agent (ARC-AGI-3, Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 + ARC3-Inference harness). The agent mines deterministic transition rules from observed frames, mechanically verifies each candidate rule by replaying recorded same-level transitions, and plans with BFS over the certified rule set at ZERO LLM tokens per action, with per-level fallback to a certified baseline agent. A level-instance is abandoned to fallback if it accumulates MAX_BREAKS_PER_LEVEL=3 prediction breaks OR if len(verified_moves()) < MIN_VERIFIED_MOVES (exec_wm.py:1066-1067, one condition, two disjuncts, ONE SHARED LABEL).
summary: The arm read NULL and for two days the null was attributed to the BREAK latch punishing a suspected frame-layer defect. That attribution is REFUTED by its own artifact. The prediction-BREAK latch fired ZERO times; MAX_BREAKS_PER_LEVEL=3 was reached exactly once in the whole run and via the unrelated sprite-lost path; both level-instances LABELLED prediction-breaks actually fell back at breaks=1 through the second disjunct. Raising or re-shaping the break threshold would have changed 0 of 31 fallbacks. The real cause is DATA STARVATION: 26 of 32 level-instances fell back at no-verified-model and 9 of 18 games produced ZERO usable transitions despite 16-20 probes executed per level. Where data existed the world model was accurate: retrodiction 810/818 = 0.990 pooled, 124/132 = 0.939 excluding the one game supplying 686 of the 818, and one level was cleared by pure BFS with zero LLM tokens.
lesson: Instrument your mechanism so that HAVING NO EVIDENCE is itself a loud result. This null hid for two days because the failure rendered as 'fell back, baseline ran, score normal' - silent - whereas a retrodiction ratio would have shown a 0/0 denominator on day one. Second, and more transferable: a gate can be broken not only by never firing but by REPORTING SOMEONE ELSE'S FIRING AS ITS OWN. One code path with two disjuncts and one shared reason string caused every downstream reader to reason about a counter that had never engaged. Give each disjunct its own label. Third: verify a diagnosis against the artifact before building the repair it implies - the repair proposed on the strength of the wrong diagnosis (convert the latching break threshold to a retrodiction ratio) would have changed nothing, though the same repair is independently justified for a DIFFERENT reason (a game retrodicting 16/16 = 1.000 was discarded because only 1 of its 4 verified rules was a MOVE and the gate demands 2 verified moves).
why_informative: This null rules OUT the world-model mechanism as the point of failure and rules IN the observation layer that feeds it. The model is not wrong - it is starved. That is a sharply different research direction from 'executable world models do not work on interactive benchmarks', which is what the naive reading of the score would have supported. It also establishes that the per-level fallback design is safe: the arm degraded to its baseline without damage (lc 25 vs baseline 28 at n=1 against an MDE of 11.1 - indistinguishable). Anyone building rule-mining or program-synthesis agents against an interactive environment should take from this that transition EXTRACTION, not rule VERIFICATION, is the likely bottleneck, and should instrument the extraction denominator before spending compute on the synthesis side.

measured.max_breaks_threshold_reached: exactly 1 time, via sprite-lost path, not the prediction path

robustness: Fallback-reason counts machine-verified by grep over the pulled kernel log plus stdout.log (raw concatenated counts 52/6/4 halved because both logs carry the same lines), independently matching a separate hand tally. Board pressure explicitly discounted: the certified baseline config itself drew 1.14 the night after this arm drew 1.05 (baseline config n=6, mean 1.5033, sd 0.3010), so the board draw is not distinguishable from its own comparator and was not used in this ruling.
instrument_mis_specification: YES, and it is load-bearing: the fallback reason string 'prediction-breaks' is emitted for BOTH disjuncts of a single condition, so two level-instances that fell back for having too few verified moves were reported as having broken their predictions. This mislabelling, not the mechanism, is what produced two consecutive days of incorrect diagnosis in the campaign's own briefs. THIS IS AN INSTRUMENT DEFECT, and the mechanism finding above is stated net of it.
sealed_reading_rule: The prereg's decisive-kill clause was conditioned on BREAK clustering on level-completing steps. That condition is refuted, so THE KILL CLAUSE DOES NOT FIRE. Equally the arm is NOT re-seeded: the failure is deterministic, not stochastic (26/32 level-instances died at the same upstream step), so a second seed reproduces it. Ruling: RE-SCOPE to 'repair the observation layer, then re-seed', CPU-only and slot-free, in order: (1) replay retained events.jsonl to find why transition extraction returns empty in 9/18 games; (2) replace the binary verified_moves()>=2 gate with a retrodiction-ratio gate; (3) split the mislabelled reason string and add game_id to log lines; (4) only then spend a slot.
